title: How Do Enzymes Work? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
Chew plain rice for a minute and it starts to taste sweet, with nothing added. Diya asks: how can starch break down so fast at body temperature? And what is doing the work?

We meet enzymes and ribozymes, zoom from a cell to an enzyme to its active site, and follow one catalytic cycle step by step: E + S to ES to EP to E + P. Then the energy hill and activation energy, enzymes vs inorganic catalysts, reaction rate and a metabolic pathway with a pause and think, a worked example on how much faster carbonic anhydrase is, the exam trap about enzymes being used up, an original NEET pattern statement question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 73 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE), PUC (Karnataka) and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 Why chewed rice tastes sweet
0:31 What is an enzyme?
0:48 Zoom ladder: cell, enzyme, active site
1:11 One catalytic cycle
1:45 The energy hill: activation energy
2:08 Enzymes vs inorganic catalysts
2:25 Rate and metabolic pathways + pause and think
3:01 Worked example: carbonic anhydrase
3:27 Exam trap: is the enzyme used up?
3:46 Practice question (NEET pattern)
4:11 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Factors Affecting Enzyme Activity, Classification and Cofactors. Why does an enzyme stop working when it is too hot, too cold, or blocked by a look-alike?
